decision: Extend the released process-record workload with explicit semantic witnesses and complete availability accounting. Attribute the established workload-design and mutation-testing ideas to their primary sources.

sources.title: SemBench: A Benchmark for Semantic Query Processing Engines
sources.examined: Native PDF text: abstract, introduction and workload-design passages on printed pages 1754–1756. The local excerpt also preserves the first six PDF pages for traceability.
sources.established_contribution: SemBench organizes 55 queries across five scenarios and three modalities, with semantic filters, joins, mapping, ranking and classification. Scenario data and existing annotations provide ground truth. It already establishes explicit operator and scenario variation as a benchmark-design principle.
sources.relation_to_this_study: The present work instantiates ordinary relational distinctions over released source-bound process records. Its measured availability and record-specific distinguishing witnesses supplement this resource. Operator variety itself is established prior work.

sources.title: Unstructured Data Analysis Using LLMs: A Comprehensive Benchmark
sources.examined: Native PDF text: abstract, introduction and design goals on printed pages 2398–2400; operator definitions in the extracted first six PDF pages.
sources.established_contribution: Bench-U defines structured ground truth for six unstructured datasets and 608 queries. Its design explicitly varies operator composition and selectivity, and includes extraction, filtering, joining and aggregation. Mixed queries combine at least three operator types.
sources.relation_to_this_study: Ground truth and composed analytical workloads are established designs. This study adds a concrete conjunction-then-grouping instance and named semantic-error witnesses to the existing process-record resource. It evaluates recorded distinctions within that resource's schema.

sources.title: Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-SQL with Distilled Test Suites
sources.examined: Official ACL primary PDF, pages 1–4, especially Sections 2, 3.1, 3.2 and 4.
sources.established_contribution: The paper formalizes distinguishing SQL queries by execution outputs, generates neighbor queries by local changes including dropped spans, and distills generated databases that distinguish those neighbors. It explains why agreement on one database permits incorrect queries with the same observed output.
sources.relation_to_this_study: Query mutation, distinguishing data and coverage through neighbors are prior ideas. Here the five released databases remain immutable; actual record-set witnesses determine which specified distinctions exist, and absent witnesses remain explicit. This produces a resource-specific sensitivity measurement.

scope_statement: The contribution is the auditable, measured semantic coverage of released documentary process records: all eligible pools, deterministic anchors, complete set outputs, and every unavailable cell. The study reports actual output distinctions for named mistakes. It supplies neither a new SQL-equivalence algorithm nor model-accuracy or engineer-population estimates.
